item.title: Outgoing legislative president calls on newly elected lawmakers to help gov’t tackle Tai Po fire aftermath
item.description: The outgoing president of Hong Kong’s legislature has urged the 90 newly elected lawmakers to “spare no effort” in helping the government tackle the aftermath of the deadly Tai Po fire. item.title: National Para Games: Hong Kong swimmers win more gold, silver; table tennis stars take most medals
item.description: A pair of Hong Kong swimmers have clinched gold and silver medals in the women’s 100-metre breaststroke at the National Games for Persons with Disabilities. Cheung Ho-ying nabbed gold on Wednesday in Shenzhen, breaking the national record with a time of one minute and 19.51 seconds, according to RTHK. Chan Yui-lam, who followed 0.64 seconds […]

item.title: UN troubled by Hong Kong clampdown after deadly Tai Po fire
item.description: The United Nations voiced alarm Tuesday at reports that Hong Kong’s “draconian” national security laws were being used against people seeking a transparent inquiry into the Chinese city’s worst fire in decades. The death toll from last month’s apartment complex blaze rose to 160 after an additional body was identified, police said on Tuesday, adding […]

item.title: Tsing Yi Nature Trails closed after 5 hikers contract chikungunya fever; robot dogs deployed to spray area
item.description: The Hong Kong government has closed access to the Tsing Yi Nature Trails after five visitors contracted the chikungunya virus, raising the number of local cases to 10. The five local cases of chikungunya fever involve two men and three women aged between 49 and 67, the Centre for Health Protection (CHP) said in a […]

item.title: Flat owners hit by Tai Po fire to get HK$100,000 relief payment
item.description: Owners of Wang Fuk Court flats affected by the fatal fire will receive a HK$100,000 payment from authorities, a senior Hong Kong government official has said. Deputy Chief Secretary Warner Cheuk announced at a Wednesday press conference the one-off payment from the government’s relief fund, the Support Fund for Wang Fuk Court in Tai Po, […]

item.title: Beijing protests ‘political’ UK sanctions on 2 Chinese cyber firms
item.description: Beijing denounced on Wednesday British sanctions on two Chinese companies which London alleged were involved in cyber activities against Britain, saying the measure amounted to “political manipulation” of security issues. item.title: Some Hong Kong events resume after mourning period for Tai Po fire victims
item.description: Some of Hong Kong’s suspended activities and events have resumed this week, following a period of mourning for the victims of the Wang Fuk Court fire, which occurred two weeks ago. “A Symphony of Lights,” the nightly laser light show across Victoria Harbour, resumed on Wednesday evening after a two-week suspension, according to the Tourism […]

item.title: Senior police inspector dies week after losing consciousness during diving test for elite tactical squad
item.description: A senior police inspector has died almost a week after losing consciousness during a diving test for the force’s elite tactical squad. item.title: Hong Kong Judiciary, Legal Aid Dep’t to prioritise cases linked to Tai Po fire victims
item.description: Hong Kong’s Judiciary and the city’s Legal Aid Department will prioritise the handling of cases linked to victims and survivors of the Tai Po fire, which has claimed at least 160 lives and burned the homes of thousands. item.title: Japan, NATO share ‘grave concern’ over China, Russia flights, Tokyo says
item.description: NATO chief Mark Rutte and Japan’s defence minister shared their “grave concerns” about recent joint patrols by Chinese and Russian aircraft, Tokyo said.
